title: Japan's Latest Tourism Trend Getting Better Sleep
paragraphs: Most people travel to see new places or try new food. But in Japan, more and more hotels are offering a different reason to travel: getting a good night's sleep.

This trend is called "sleep tourism," and it means taking a trip mainly to rest and sleep well. According to news reports, a growing number of hotels in Japan now offer special stays that help guests sleep better. One travel expert from the Japanese travel company JTB said this is because many people are unhappy with the quality of their sleep and are interested in health.

One example is the Malibu Hotel in Zushi, a seaside town about one hour from central Tokyo. In February 2026, the hotel started a plan called SLEEP WELL STAY. Before guests go to bed, they talk about how they like to sleep, and then they choose a mattress that suits them. Guests can also use special pillows, wear clothes that help the body rest and sleep on silk pillow covers. The room has soft lights and relaxing music, and guests can drink herbal tea before bed. In the morning, they can do yoga by the sea. The plan costs an extra 12,500 yen per person.

Other hotels are also joining the trend. For example, Hotel Chinzanso Tokyo uses a machine to measure how well guests sleep. Tokyo Prince Hotel also has a plan to help guests relax and sleep without their phones.

But travelers do not need to stay in expensive hotels to sleep well in Japan. Many travelers also enjoy quiet nights at ryokan, traditional Japanese inns, often in hot spring towns. Some people even stay at temples, where they can eat simple vegetarian food and join morning prayers. Others choose capsule hotels with lights that slowly get darker at bedtime and brighter in the morning.
